title: Governance review: project export
description: One project as written by 'Download project data (JSON)', from the published build (CHAI, 'chai-review/2') or a build of any other framework ('<id>-review/<n>', D-79). The structure is the same for every framework; where a value comes from the framework's definition (its item ids, statuses, categories, phases and checkpoints), this schema states it for the published framework only, under the 'chai-review/2' condition at the end (D-82). Fields other than _state are derived for convenience; import reads _state. tests/test_export_schema.py validates real exports against this file, and also with every object closed, so a field the export writes and this file does not describe fails.

schema.description: The framework's export id: 'chai-review/2' for the published build, the definition's export.schemaId for any other (the pattern is the one schema/framework.schema.json gives it).

project_id.description: The id of the project this was exported from. Part of what the fingerprint covers, so a reader can recompute it. Import ignores it and creates a new project.

fingerprint.description: Identifies this exact version of the record, so a report or a filed copy can be tied to it. MD5 is a version fingerprint only; SHA-256 is the digest to quote if a hash is ever offered as evidence that a record was not altered. Recompute with examples/load_export.py (verify_fingerprint). Absent in older exports (#150).

storage.description: Where the record was kept when this was exported, so a filed copy carries its own provenance (#93). Absent in older exports.

mode.description: 'artifact' was a mode of earlier versions (a Claude artifact); it is no longer produced, and is accepted so older exports still validate.

status.description: The engine's, the same for every framework.

phase.description: The label of one of the framework's phases, or 'Retired' or 'Stopped'.

msg.description: The dashboard's catalog key for the flag and its parameters, which the dashboard uses to show it in the reader's language. The key is the dashboard's, not a stable identifier; read text.

model_card.description: The published framework's applied model card. Absent from another framework's export.

id.description: The item's id in the framework's definition.

stage.description: The number of the item's section.

principle.description: The id of the item's category.

status.description: One of the framework's status values, or null when unanswered.

references.description: Evidence references: links and file fingerprints. A file is never included, only its name, size and SHA-256.

url.description: An http or https address, or null.

scores.description: Readiness in percent: overall, and one per category id of the framework.

_state.description: The stored project document. This is what import reads.

items.description: The primary framework's answers, keyed by item id.

access.description: Who may open the project, by user id. Empty lists mean unrestricted.

additionalProperties.description: Any other key is a supplementary framework's record, under its id (OPTICA's is 'optica').

chaiUseCase.description: CHAI use case slug whose Testing & Evaluation framework this project draws suggested metrics from. Empty in another framework's export.

framework.description: The build's primary framework, stamped on every record a build of other frameworks makes (R-67). Absent from the published build's records, which are CHAI's.

gates.description: Checkpoint decisions, keyed by the framework's checkpoint ids.

enabled.description: Whether the project uses it (an opt-in supplement such as OPTICA).

answers.description: Its answers, keyed by its item ids.

chai.description: What the published framework's definition (app/frameworks/chai/framework.json) fixes. tests/test_export_schema.py checks each list here against the definition.

principle.description: U usefulness, F fairness, S safety, T transparency, P security & privacy
